user.title: Generic Water Heater Setup
user.description:
Creates a virtual water heater that controls a switch using a temperature sensor.

Modes:
- electric: heats normally using target temperature and tolerances.
- performance (Boost): prioritizes heating.

Smart Eco is controlled with a dedicated select entity and uses the template below as the allow/block condition for heating.

Enable Debug Logging to capture detailed decision paths and state transitions in Home Assistant logs.

temperatures.name: Temperatures
temperatures.description: Target step, tolerances and the range the heater may be set to.

cycle_protection.name: Cycle protection
cycle_protection.description: Minimum on and off times, to stop the element short-cycling.

smart_eco.name: Smart Eco
smart_eco.description: The condition that decides when heating is allowed, and how long a manual override pauses it.

data_description.eco_mode_template_condition: Boolean template used by Smart Eco policy. Smart Eco policy is controlled by a select entity with modes Off, Off until target reached, On until next manual control, Auto Resume after Delay, and Always ON.
data_description.smart_eco_manual_off_resume_hours: In Smart Eco Mode 'Auto Resume after Delay', manual OFF pauses Smart Eco policy for this many hours before automatic resumption. It is also the bound on 'Off until target reached': if the tank never reaches target, Smart Eco is restored after this long rather than staying down indefinitely.

fleet.name: Fleet coordination
fleet.description: Stops several heaters stepping on together. Nominal power is the PEAK draw, used for the shared watt budget.

data_description.nominal_power_w: The element's PEAK draw, not its average. 0 means unknown and excludes this heater from the budget.
data_description.fleet_stagger_seconds: Minimum spacing between this heater switching on and any other Generic Water Heater instance switching on. Stops several heaters stepping onto a shared inverter or generator in the same instant when they react to the same trigger. A blocked heater waits and retries; it is never skipped. The largest value set on any instance applies to the whole fleet. 0 disables staggering.
data_description.fleet_power_budget_w: Maximum combined nominal power that all Generic Water Heater instances may have switched on at once. 0 disables the budget. The smallest non-zero value set on any instance applies to the whole fleet. A heater is never blocked while no other instance is drawing, so this can only prevent a combined overload, never leave you without hot water entirely.

legionella.name: Legionella
legionella.description: Thermal-conditions tracking, and the policy select that runs a disinfection cycle. 'Disinfect' waits for the eco condition; 'Disinfect ASAP' stands Smart Eco down until the tank gets there.

data_description.enable_legionella_sensor: Adds a sensor reporting how favourable this tank's recent temperature history has been to Legionella growth, and how long since it last reached a disinfection temperature. It is a thermal-conditions index computed from ONE sensor at ONE height -- not a measurement of contamination. It cannot see the coldest water in the tank, sediment, biofilm, or any outlet downstream; only a laboratory test can tell you what is in the water. A qualifying cycle is 60 °C held for one continuous hour at the sensor. That threshold is fixed on purpose: below 60 °C a cycle is not a gentler version of the same thing and can leave the tank worse than before.
data_description.legionella_interval_days: How long a completed disinfection cycle counts for before the sensor reports Elevated, and twice that before it reports High. Guidance that prescribes a cycle at all asks for daily in institutional systems; single-family homes are largely outside the scope of those standards, and shipped appliance controllers use anywhere from 3 to 30 days.
data_description.enable_max_temp_history_sensor: Adds a sensor under the same device that tracks the highest recorded temperature over the last 7 days. Disabled by default.

hot_water_in_use.name: Hot water in use
hot_water_in_use.description: Detects a draw from this tank's own temperature falling faster than standing loss allows.

data.enable_hot_water_in_use: Create a Hot Water In Use sensor

data_description.enable_hot_water_in_use: The detector works on this tank's temperature alone; the entity below is optional and only makes it more sensitive.
data_description.water_in_use_entity: A whole-house 'water is flowing' entity. Optional. It corroborates the milder falls that temperature alone cannot settle — it never gates detection, and a steep fall is reported without it.

data_description.enable_debug_logging: Logs detailed runtime diagnostics, including mode transitions, heating/idle state transitions, threshold decisions, eco condition updates, manual overrides, and switch command/cooldown reasoning. Disabled by default.
